acceptedAnswer.text: Prompt caching is an architectural capability that allows developers to reuse frequently referenced context across consecutive API requests: Up to 90% Cost Reduction: Reading from cached prompt tokens costs up to 90% less than base input token rates, dramatically reducing expenses for repetitive system prompts and long context bases. Up to 80% Latency Improvement: By eliminating redundant context processing on cached blocks, Time to First Token (TTFT) drops significantly on long-document queries. Strategic Cache Breakpoints: Position cache control blocks at predictable boundaries - system instructions, API tool schemas, standard operating procedures, and codebase snapshots. 5-Minute & 1-Hour TTL Options: Optimize memory retention based on request frequency to maximize cache hit ratios across multi-turn user sessions and agent swarms. Our training equips your team to structure prompts for maximum cache efficiency, achieving business-scale throughput with minimal spend.
